title: Beta rollout plan + feature flags for SIEM-ready audit export (tenant allowlist, staged enablement, rollback)
creator: Connor O'Brien
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation — SIEM-ready audit export (Beta)
description:
Goal
Ship a safe, reversible, staged beta rollout mechanism for “SIEM-ready audit export” across Hosted + Dedicated tenants. This ticket defines the feature-flag strategy (control plane + exporter), tenant allowlist management, and rollback procedures with SRE/Release.

Background / Why
Audit export has meaningful compliance/security implications and non-trivial operational risk (downstream throttling, customer misconfiguration, data volume spikes). We need:
- Hard gating behind a kill-switch and per-tenant allowlist
- A staged rollout plan (internal alpha → 3–5 beta accounts) with explicit enablement steps
- A rollback plan that is quick (minutes), minimizes data duplication, and has clear on-call playbooks

Non-goals
- GA rollout mechanics (broad self-serve enablement) — will be follow-up after beta learnings.
- Private/on-prem rollout strategy — explicitly out of scope for beta (documented elsewhere).

Feature flags (authoritative definitions)
1) Global kill switch
- Flag: audit_export.enabled_global
- Owner: Releases/SRE
- Default: false in all envs until internal alpha signoff
- Behavior: when false, control plane rejects create/update/test export config (HTTP 404 or 403 per API design), exporter stops polling and pauses all deliveries.

2) Per-tenant allowlist gating
- Flag: audit_export.enabled_tenants_allowlist
- Representation: tenant IDs in allowlist store + cached in control plane; exporter also receives allowlist signal to fail-closed.
- Behavior:
  - Control plane: export config CRUD + status endpoints only usable for allowlisted tenants
  - Exporter: even if it receives configs, it should no-op if tenant not allowlisted (defense-in-depth)

3) Destination-type gating (for phased adapter rollout)
- Flags:
  - audit_export.destination.s3_enabled
  - audit_export.destination.splunk_hec_enabled
  - audit_export.destination.datadog_logs_enabled
- Default plan:
  - S3 first (lowest integration coupling) → Splunk HEC → Datadog Logs

4) Backfill/replay safety gating
- Flag: audit_export.backfill_enabled
- Default: false initially; beta to ship with limited backfill window (per PRD) and explicit operator controls.

5) “Auto-pause on max lag” (safety control)
- Flag: audit_export.autopause_on_max_lag
- Default: true for beta
- Behavior: exporter pauses tenant delivery when max lag threshold exceeded (prevents runaway retries and protects queues).

Enablement & allowlist management
- Source of truth: Control plane “feature gating” service.
- Admin tooling:
  - CLI (internal) for adding/removing tenant IDs from allowlist
  - Audit trail: every allowlist change must emit an audit event (category: security / admin) including actor + tenant + change type.
- Operational process:
  1) PM (Naomi) confirms beta customer selection
  2) Support/CS files internal request (INT-9012) with tenant ID(s), destinations, region, and planned date/time
  3) Release lead (Connor) applies allowlist update during a maintenance window or coordinated time
  4) SRE validates health dashboards and confirms status endpoint shows “enabled + delivering”

Staged rollout plan
Phase 0 — Dev + Staging validation
- Enable audit_export.enabled_global only in staging
- Run e2e integration tests (ENG-5195) against Splunk/Datadog stubs + S3 test buckets
- Confirm:
  - No events delivered when tenant not allowlisted (fail-closed)
  - Status endpoint reflects “disabled_by_flag” vs “no_config” correctly

Phase 1 — Internal alpha (1–2 Redwood internal tenants)
- Enable global flag in prod, but allowlist only internal tenants
- Destination flags: s3_enabled=true, splunk/datadog=false
- Observe for 72h:
  - Export lag SLO signal and error budget burn
  - Exporter CPU/mem + queue depth
  - No PII violations in exporter logs (spot-check)

Phase 2 — Limited beta (3–5 external accounts)
- Add customer tenants to allowlist one-by-one with a minimum 24h soak between enables
- For each tenant:
  - Start with S3 (if acceptable), then Splunk or Datadog based on customer stack
  - Confirm customer-side dedup guidance (at-least-once) is communicated
  - Schedule weekly check-in with CS (Miguel) + SE (Colin/Simran)

Phase 3 — Expand within beta cohort (optional)
- If SLOs stable and support load acceptable, expand allowlist within the pre-approved beta customer shortlist only.

Rollback strategy (must be executable in < 10 minutes)
Rollback level 1: Per-tenant disable
- Remove tenant from allowlist
- Expected result:
  - Control plane hides/blocks config operations
  - Exporter stops delivery for that tenant within config sync interval
- Use when: single customer experiencing issues (bad token, throttling, unexpected volume)

Rollback level 2: Destination adapter disable
- Flip audit_export.destination.<type>_enabled=false
- Expected result:
  - Exporter pauses only that adapter (for all tenants) and marks destination health as “disabled_by_flag”
- Use when: adapter bug or upstream changes (e.g., Splunk HEC behavior)

Rollback level 3: Global kill switch
- Flip audit_export.enabled_global=false
- Expected result:
  - All deliveries stop; status endpoint shows globally disabled
- Use when: systemic issues, suspected data leakage, incident requiring immediate stop

Data-consistency expectations during rollback
- Delivery semantics are at-least-once; downstream SIEM must deduplicate by event_id.
- Rollback does not delete checkpoints; re-enable may replay from last committed checkpoint (possible duplicates).
- If a customer claims “missing events,” use status endpoint + lag metrics and DLQ tooling; do not assume loss without checking checkpoint state.

SRE / Release requirements
- Paging criteria: global kill switch usage should be paired with incident declaration if customer-facing.
- Add “rollout checklist” to release train runbook:
  - Confirm flags set as intended (global + destination + backfill)
  - Confirm allowlist entries
  - Confirm dashboards: lag p95, delivery success rate, adapter 4xx/5xx, retry rates
  - Confirm status endpoint cache TTL and tenancy checks are healthy

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Flags defined and documented with owners + defaults
- [x] Control plane rejects/blocks non-allowlisted tenants (fail-closed)
- [x] Exporter also fails-closed for non-allowlisted tenants
- [x] Rollback procedures written and validated in staging
- [x] Internal alpha + at least one external beta enablement executed using this process

Implementation notes / links
- Control plane allowlist + kill switch implementation: https://sources/github/redwood/pr-28824-feature-flag-tenant-allowlist-for-siem-export-beta.json
- Status endpoint supporting UI/ops validation: https://sources/github/redwood/pr-28805-add-audit-export-status-endpoint-and-health.json
- SRE dashboards/alerts: https://sources/github/observability-pack/pr-392-add-audit-exporter-dashboards-and-alerts.json
- Relevant SRE runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-audit-exporter-delivery-failures.json
- PRD / beta criteria: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/siem-ready-audit-export-beta-prd.json

Risks / open questions (resolved during implementation)
- Q: Should we allow config CRUD but block delivery for non-allowlisted tenants?
  - Decision: No. Beta should be invisible unless enabled; reduces support burden and prevents accidental misconfiguration.
- Q: Where should gating be enforced?
  - Decision: Both control plane and exporter (defense in depth).

Comms / enablement
- Internal enablement request path documented in #announcements and Internal Support (INT-9012)
- Sales/SE guidance: direct customers to beta scope disclaimers (no Private) and at-least-once semantics
